results.claim: National legal cannabis sales were approximately $5 billion in 2023.
results.explanation: Multiple authoritative industry sources place 2023 U.S. legal cannabis sales dramatically higher than $5 billion. MJBizDaily (mjbizdaily.com/us-cannabis-sales-estimates/) reported combined medical and recreational sales could reach $33.6 billion by end of 2023, while the MJBiz Factbook (mjbizdaily.com/cannabis-industry-will-add-100-billion-to-us-economy-in-2023/) projected $34 billion for 2023 (up from a revised $30 billion in 2022). Whitney Economics (cannabisbusinesstimes.com) projected 2024 legal sales of $31.4 billion representing 9.1% growth over 2023, implying ~$28.8 billion in 2023. Cannabusinessplans.com similarly cited 2023 sales of 'almost $30 billion.' The claimed figure of ~$5 billion is off by roughly 6x the widely cited estimates, making this a material factual error with high severity for any investment decision.

results.claim: Passage of initiatives in California, Nevada, Massachusetts, Maine, Florida, Arkansas, Montana and North Dakota will add $7.4 billion to the 2029 market forecast.
results.explanation: The states listed — California, Nevada, Massachusetts, Maine, Florida, Arkansas, Montana, and North Dakota — correspond exactly to the eight states that passed cannabis ballot initiatives in November 2016. However, authoritative industry sources materially contradict both key data points in the claim. Gray-Robinson LLP (gray-robinson.com), citing industry research, states those 2016 initiatives would produce new markets of $7.1 billion — not $7.4 billion — and that figure was projected by 2020, not 2029. Cannabis Business Times (cannabisbusinesstimes.com) independently corroborates the $7.1B figure and 2020 horizon, citing the Arcview Market Research / New Frontier Data 'State of Legal Marijuana Markets' report. The $7.4 billion figure does appear in New Frontier Data's post-2020-election analysis (newfrontierdata.com), but in a completely different context: it refers to the 2020 adult-use sales baseline growing to $25.1B by 2025, not an incremental contribution from the 2016 ballot states to a 2029 forecast. No authoritative source reviewed supports the combination of $7.4B and a 2029 horizon tied specifically to these eight 2016 initiative states. The claim appears to conflate or misstate both the dollar amount and the forecast year.
results.missing_information: A primary industry report (e.g., Arcview/New Frontier Data 'State of Legal Marijuana Markets' post-November 2016 edition or a comparable BDS Analytics / BDSA long-range forecast through 2029) explicitly modeling the incremental market contribution of the eight 2016 ballot-initiative states through 2029 would be needed to determine whether any version of this figure is supportable at that time horizon.

results.claim: Recreational cannabis sales will account for more than 53% of the overall market by 2029.
results.explanation: Multiple authoritative sources broadly support the claim, though the exact 53% threshold is actually conservative relative to current US data. Grand View Research (grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/us-cannabis-market) reports that the recreational use segment already held a 66.9% revenue share of the US cannabis market in 2024 and is projected to grow at the fastest CAGR through 2030, meaning the >53% threshold is readily exceeded for the US market. Statista (statista.com/outlook/hmo/cannabis/recreational-cannabis/united-states) projects US recreational cannabis to reach $30.12bn by 2029 out of a ~$75bn global total, and bizplanr.ai (citing Statista) indicates global recreational revenue reached ~$38.32bn in 2025, suggesting recreational's global share is also near or above 50%. Straits Research and SkyQuest both note that the recreational segment "dominated" the global cannabis market and is expected to register the highest CAGR. The one meaningful caveat is that Grand View Research's global legal cannabis report (grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/legal-cannabis-market) shows the medical segment at 63.56% globally in 2024, implying recreational is only ~36% on a strictly global basis — so the verdict depends heavily on whether the claim refers to the US or global market. For a US-focused operator, the claim is well-supported and even understates the recreational share already achieved.
results.missing_information: The claim does not specify US vs. global scope. A primary industry report (e.g., MJBiz Factbook, Statista Cannabis Outlook, or BDSA) that explicitly projects recreational's percentage share of the total market by 2029 — rather than absolute dollar figures — would allow a more precise validation.

results.claim: The legal cannabis market would see $22.8 billion in total annual sales by 2029.
results.explanation: Every authoritative source reviewed places the legal cannabis market well above $22.8 billion — not just by 2029, but already today. Whitney Economics (via cannabis.lacity.gov) reported U.S. legal cannabis sales alone hit $30.1 billion in 2024, already exceeding the claim's 2029 target. Grand View Research (grandviewresearch.com) estimated the U.S. market at $38.50 billion in 2024 and projects an 11.51% CAGR through 2030. BDSA (cited by cannabissciencetech.com) forecasts U.S. regulated cannabis sales — adult use plus medical — reaching $39.1 billion by 2029, with adult-use alone at $23.9 billion in 2025. Statista and Paybotic Financial (payboticfinancial.com) put the U.S. legal cannabis market at $45.3 billion in 2025. For the global market, Statista projects $75.09 billion by 2029 (bizplanr.ai). No source — U.S.-only or global — supports a figure as low as $22.8 billion by 2029; the claim dramatically understates the current market baseline and all forward projections.

results.claim: There are 583 licensed cultivations for retail marijuana as of August 1, 2025.
results.explanation: No authoritative source found that explicitly corroborates a count of exactly 583 licensed retail marijuana cultivation facilities as of August 1, 2025. The most comparable public data comes from Colorado — the most documented retail marijuana market — where the Colorado Department of Revenue (DOR) records cited by Westword and MJBiz Daily (mjbizdaily.com) report approximately 488 active recreational cultivation licenses as of December 2025, and the Colorado Marijuana Enforcement Division's (MED) 2025 Regulatory & Enforcement Update (med.colorado.gov, published February 2026, cited by themarijuanaherald.com) places the year-end figure at 478 retail cultivations. These end-of-2025 figures are materially lower (~17–18%) than the claimed 583, and the DOR itself documented a 48% decline in recreational cultivation licenses from 2021 to 2025. While the August 2025 count would naturally be higher than the December 2025 count given the declining trend, the gap between 583 and ~488 over roughly five months (August–December 2025) would imply an unusually steep acceleration of closures not corroborated by any available dataset. The state to which this figure applies is also unspecified in the claim, and no nationwide or other state-level source returns a comparable figure of 583.
results.missing_information: A real-time or point-in-time snapshot of retail marijuana cultivation licenses as of August 1, 2025 from the Colorado MED Licensee Information and Lookup Tool (med.colorado.gov/licensee-information-and-lookup-tool) or equivalent state regulatory authority would be required to confirm or refute the specific figure. The claim also does not identify the jurisdiction, which would require clarification before any authoritative single-source lookup is possible.

results.claim: Deal sizes for indoor flower range from 0.5 to 100 pounds.
results.explanation: Multiple authoritative sources corroborate the broad 0.5–100 lb deal-size range for indoor cannabis flower. On the lower bound, wholesalecbdflowershop.com explicitly lists offerings from '1/2 LB – 100 LBS,' and several wholesale platforms (Green Unicorn Farms, ShopZaza, Rogue Origin) all advertise half-pound (0.5 lb) minimum purchases for indoor flower. On the upper bound, 25hourfarms.com references orders up to 100 lbs, and wholesalecbdflowershop.com again matches the 100 lb ceiling. Cannabis Benchmarks (cannabisbenchmarks.com) provides the most granular B2B data: average *forward* deal sizes for indoor-grown flower have ranged from ~29 lbs (September 2021) to ~69 lbs (July 2022), squarely within the stated range; average *spot* deal sizes are much smaller at ~2.4–2.5 lbs per transaction, also within range. The 0.5–100 lb window is therefore broadly representative of typical B2B transaction sizes, though very large bulk operators can transact above 100 lbs. The claim is not materially contradicted by any source found.
results.assumed_industry: Cannabis cultivation and retail (legal cannabis business)

results.claim: Deal sizes for greenhouse flower range from 1 to 320 pounds.
results.explanation: No authoritative industry source specifically corroborates a deal-size range of 1–320 pounds for greenhouse cannabis flower. The most relevant data comes from Cannabis Benchmarks® (cannabisbenchmarks.com), which tracks wholesale cannabis transactions: their weekly U.S. Cannabis Spot Index reports show average spot deal sizes of roughly 2–2.5 pounds and average forward deal sizes for greenhouse flower ranging from ~21 pounds (January 2021) to ~96 pounds (mid-2022), far below the claimed 320-pound upper bound. While wholesale platforms (e.g., wholesalecbdflower.com, greenunicornfarms.com) confirm that 1-pound minimum orders are standard in the market—supporting the lower bound—no source documents 320 pounds as an industry-typical upper limit for a single greenhouse flower deal. The claim's specific range is therefore not corroborated by available data.
results.missing_information: Transaction-level distribution data (minimum, maximum, and full range of individual deal sizes) for greenhouse flower would be needed—such as Cannabis Benchmarks® premium subscription reports or state-level regulatory transaction data from mature markets (e.g., Colorado MED, Oregon OLCC) that capture the full dispersion of wholesale order sizes, not just averages.

results.claim: Deal sizes for outdoor flower range from 1 to 200 pounds.
results.explanation: The claim that outdoor cannabis flower deal sizes range from 1 to 200 pounds is broadly consistent with authoritative industry data. Cannabis Benchmarks (cannabisbenchmarks.com), the most credible U.S. wholesale cannabis price-reporting agency, consistently reports average forward deal sizes for outdoor flower between 43 lbs (September 2019) and 96 lbs (July 2022) across multiple reporting periods — placing 200 lbs at roughly twice the average, a plausible upper bound for larger wholesale transactions within a realistic distribution. Spot-market deal averages reported by Cannabis Benchmarks are much smaller (~2.5 lbs), confirming that the lower end of the 1-lb claim is realistic. CannDelta (canndelta.com), a cannabis licensing consultancy, independently corroborates the low end, noting 'some allow orders as small as 1–5 pounds.' Multiple wholesale platforms (e.g., Hemp Living Wholesale, ShopZaza) also confirm pound-level minimum purchases. No single authoritative source explicitly defines 200 lbs as the precise ceiling, but the overall 1–200 lb range is consistent with the distribution implied by Cannabis Benchmarks' averages.
